name: manual_e8d8ee
claim: semgrep Bash language support (marked experimental by semgrep's own blog) does not reliably expose quoted strings as a distinct string-literal AST node -- a bare metavariable captures a quoted value INCLUDING its surrounding quotes as part of a generic expression match, while the literal-metavariable quoted syntax (meant to match string literals and strip the quotes) silently matches nothing at all against real bash string assignments. Before trusting any bash-language semgrep or opengrep rule that uses that literal-metavariable quoted syntax or a nested metavariable-pattern block without an explicit generic-language override, test it empirically against real sample code -- a rule that looks syntactically correct can be a silent no-op.

decisions.notes: 2026-08-09: verified via semgrep 1.172.0 that .opengrep.yml's pt-no-hardcoded-secret-env rule (both current origin/main's version and bump-agentic-stack-vendor-pin's proposed fix) fails to match a genuine hardcoded secret assignment -- neither is a false-negative on a corner case, both are a total no-op on the textbook positive example the rule exists to catch. Root cause narrowed to Bash's experimental semgrep support not distinguishing string-literal nodes from generic expression nodes; corroborated by semgrep's own blog post explicitly stating Bash support in Semgrep is still experimental with many known bugs, and a semgrep GitHub issue (#4117) about metavariable-pattern not capturing full Bash expression content. This is a genuinely open bug in the security-tooling rule, not something fixed by either branch -- needs dedicated follow-up, not a rushed patch.
